searchText: Yes we need client specific config files. The one I provided is for Besu. I can also align with what Quilt did. As you prefer <@!552133098075193354> Got it. <@!543900561460822016> should I add what you shared above as the geth genesis? if you just rename `eip1559Block` to `aleutBlock` that should be the only thing needed Do you mean rename it directly in the `aleut.md` file as it is right now, and that this would work with both Besu and Geth? once <@!574864862338088960> updates it should i don't have a strong preference, i could also conform To be clear, is this what you meant 🤔 ? https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/29 yes looks good to me I will conform now worries https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/pull/2149 Done <@!552133098075193354> Yay! I still need to add `"petersburgBlock": 0,` to get the genesis file from https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/29 to work in geth. I'll draft a PR, with that change I'm now synced using the quilt/eip1559 branch https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/30 Is it possible that this is because Besu calls it "constantinopleFix" and Geth "petersberg"? ya that must be it, geth doesn't have a constantinopleFix block. I'm not sure about other clients but geth seems to ignore fields it doesn't understand, hopefully besu and others behave the same way and we can just make the genesis a superset of the required fields? has there been any discussion on the names of the new fields in the JSONRPC responses (e.g. in eth_getTransactionByHash). Now that I'm synced I'm trying to test end-to-end JSONRPC response -> RLP -> Hash for EIP-1559 txs but that obviously fails since the new fields aren't exposed via JSONRPC yet. I figured I can start on adding them as a PR to the quilt branch but not sure if the names have been settled on. For now my code is using `maxInclusionFee` and `maxFee` but I know I've seen baseFee and Tip used in places before too. Somewhat related, but I really wish we'd thought to add EIP-2718 style types to blocks too, casing on whether the header has 15 or 16 fields to know if BaseFee is there feels dirty.. interesting, i expected it to fallback to being the same as constantinople https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/1e207342b545fb5992e2e8f38e60f219f379e5e0/params/config.go#L324 <@!388751025789468672> btw i added the `--aleut` flag Ya it's this function that seems to have the bug https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/1e207342b545fb5992e2e8f38e60f219f379e5e0/params/config.go#L468 fix would probably be to set `c.PetersburgBlock` to `c.ConstantinopleBlock` if it's nil somewhere. I see, `feeCap` and `tip` were added to transaction_marshalling.go but the JSONRPC layer actually uses RPCTransaction (in internal/ethapi/api.go), I'll take a stab at updating RPCTransaction for EIP-1559. https://github.com/quilt/go-ethereum/pull/47 <-- with that I'm able to go from JSONRPC -> RLP -> hash on all the blocks and txs currently on Aleut using my own in-progress EIP-1559 parser. sorry didn't realize i hadn't quite published this yet I'm also taking a stab at adding `effectiveGasPrice` to `eth_getTransactionReceipt` and started to compute it based on block.baseFee and maxFee/tip, but realized this logic probably already exists somewhere since it needs to be calculated for applying the txs. But looking then I see that `DynamicFeeTransaction.gasPrice()` returns `tx.Tip`, but according to the pseudo-code in the EIP shouldn't that really return something more like `inclusion_fee_per_gas = min(transaction.max_inclusion_fee_per_gas, transaction.max_fee_per_gas - block.base_fee_per_gas)`? Ah I see, that logic is in `StateTransition` I wonder if instead of adding fee and tip to `Message` we could make `Transaction.AsMessage` do the computation? That would require passing in the block's baseFee to AsMessage though, perhaps that's too big of a change? That said, everywhere `AsMessage` is called has access to either the block or the baseFee via `EVMBlockContext` (Also if this is a distraction to this channel happy to take this dicussion elsewhere) Yeah, the consensus calculation of gas is done in `StateTransition`. I'm not super happy with the interface having `GasPrice` even for 1559 txs, but would increase the complexity in the txpool to constantly switch on the type. i think having the computation in the `StateTransition` make it more "findable" Ya looking at it more I agree, I missed that `StateTransition` already had a fair amount of per-fork complexity in `IntrinsicGas`. Anyways it was pretty straight-forward to replicate the gas-price logic in `GetTransactionReceipt`. Maybe `DynamicFeeTransaction.gasPrice()` should return some sentinel value instead of the Tip to make it more obvious it shouldn't be used? yeah maybe it just returns 0 - my thinking with tip is at least it still serves as a "priority" signal e.g. larger tip means more priority like bigger gasPrice means more priority but don't have a strong preference At a more meta level, now I'm questioning if `effectiveGasPrice` should even be part of the `eth_getTransactionReceipt` response since it's no longer a consensus field of the receipt, arguably it could go in `RPCTransaction` (for mined txs) or even be left out altogether. Which, sigh, is what you said here: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3463#issuecomment-812895257. I misread that as still adding it to `eth_getTransactionReceipt`. i really don't have a good feel if it is important to include `eth_getTransactionReceipt` - it feels like something to include in the `eth_getTransaction*` but like i said in the PR, i'm happy with what the consumers of the RPC prefer ya I agree it makes sense in `getTransaction`. Not sure if it makes sense to change the name to `effectiveGasPrice` or keep it `gasPrice`, I can see arguments either way. I updated my PR to set `gasPrice` to the effective gas price on EIP-1559s, and to add the `baseFee` to block responses. tangentially related but it'd be really nice if `eth_getBlockByNumber("pending", true)` returned the presumptive `baseFee`, currently it doesn't. <@574864862338088960> would that work with Besu? Worst case I’ll just put client-specific ones in the spec If anyone has a little Aleut ETH to spare for `0xdf0a88b2b68c673713a8ec826003676f272e3573` I'd like to try getting some txs in my pending pool to see if the JSONRPC behaves reasonably for them.

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content:
I'm also taking a stab at adding `effectiveGasPrice` to `eth_getTransactionReceipt` and started to compute it based on block.baseFee and maxFee/tip, but realized this logic probably already exists somewhere since it needs to be calculated for applying the txs.

But looking then I see that `DynamicFeeTransaction.gasPrice()` returns `tx.Tip`, but according to the pseudo-code in the EIP shouldn't that really return something more like `inclusion_fee_per_gas = min(transaction.max_inclusion_fee_per_gas, transaction.max_fee_per_gas - block.base_fee_per_gas)`?

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content: Ah I see, that logic is in `StateTransition`

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content: I wonder if instead of adding fee and tip to `Message` we could  make `Transaction.AsMessage` do the computation?  That would require passing in the block's baseFee to AsMessage though, perhaps that's too big of a change?

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content: That said, everywhere `AsMessage` is called has access to either the block or the baseFee via `EVMBlockContext`

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content: (Also if this is a distraction to this channel happy to take this dicussion elsewhere)

excerpts.content: Yeah, the consensus calculation of gas is done in `StateTransition`. I'm not super happy with the interface having `GasPrice` even for 1559 txs, but would increase the complexity in the txpool to constantly switch on the type.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: i think having the computation in the `StateTransition` make it more "findable"

excerpts.content: Ya looking at it more I agree, I missed that `StateTransition` already had a fair amount of per-fork complexity in `IntrinsicGas`.  Anyways it was pretty straight-forward to replicate the gas-price logic in `GetTransactionReceipt`.
